claim_truth.subject: Prescribers
claim_truth.evidence_quote: Prescribers can digitally sign, transmit, report, and archive electronic prescriptions, while pharmacies can receive, dispense, and archive these electronic prescriptions.

claim_truth.subject: Prescribers
claim_truth.evidence_quote: Prescribers can digitally sign, transmit, report, and archive electronic prescriptions, while pharmacies can receive, dispense, and archive these electronic prescriptions.

claim_truth.subject: Pharmacies
claim_truth.evidence_quote: while pharmacies can receive, dispense, and archive these electronic prescriptions.

claim_truth.subject: Electronic system prescriber assignment
claim_truth.object: two-factor authentication to assign a prescriber within the electronic system
claim_truth.evidence_quote: Two-factor authentication must be used to assign a prescriber within the electronic system, approve a prescription entry, and digitally sign a prescription.

claim_truth.subject: Prescription entry approval
claim_truth.object: two-factor authentication to approve a prescription entry
claim_truth.evidence_quote: Two-factor authentication must be used to assign a prescriber within the electronic system, approve a prescription entry, and digitally sign a prescription.

claim_truth.subject: Prescription digital signing
claim_truth.object: two-factor authentication to digitally sign a prescription
claim_truth.evidence_quote: Two-factor authentication must be used to assign a prescriber within the electronic system, approve a prescription entry, and digitally sign a prescription.

claim_truth.subject: Two-factor authentication factors
claim_truth.object: two of the following three options: a username/password, a hard token, or a biometric identification
claim_truth.evidence_quote: Two of the factors must be of the following three options: a username/password, a hard token, or a biometric identification.

claim_truth.subject: Token or OTP generator
claim_truth.object: the same requirements as defined for a hard token under the current regulation
claim_truth.evidence_quote: The DEA has stated that the use of a type of token or OTP generator must meet the same requirements as defined for a hard token under the current regulation.

claim_truth.subject: Hard token
claim_truth.object: FIPS 140 Security Level 1 for cryptographic devices or OTP devices
conditions: If a hard token is used
claim_truth.evidence_quote: If a hard token is used, it must meet FIPS 140 Security Level 1 for cryptographic devices or OTP devices.

claim_truth.subject: Hard token
claim_truth.object: a device that is separate from the computer being used to access the application
claim_truth.evidence_quote: The hard token must be stored on a device that is separate from the computer being used to access the application.

claim_truth.subject: Multi-factor authenticators at AAL3
claim_truth.object: hardware cryptographic modules validated at FIPS 140 Level 2 overall with at least FIPS 140 Level 3 for physical security
claim_truth.evidence_quote: According to NIST SP 800-63B Section 4.3 , multi-factor authenticators used at AAL3 shall rely on hardware cryptographic modules validated at FIPS 140 Level 2 overall with at least FIPS 140 Level 3 for physical security, which exceeds the EPCS MFA requirements.

claim_truth.subject: Verifiers at AAL3
claim_truth.evidence_quote: Verifiers at AAL3 shall be validated at FIPS 140 Level 1 or higher.

claim_truth.subject: Users
claim_truth.object: secondary verification for MFA scenarios to meet your EPCS MFA requirements with the Microsoft Authenticator app
claim_truth.evidence_quote: With the Microsoft Authenticator app, you can provide secondary verification for MFA scenarios to meet your EPCS MFA requirements.

informational_truth.subject: Electronic Prescriptions for Controlled Substances (EPCS)
informational_truth.content: A rule issued by US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) that went into effect on 1 June 2010.
informational_truth.evidence_quote: The US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Electronic Prescriptions for Controlled Substances (EPCS) is a rule that went into effect on 1 June 2010.

informational_truth.subject: Hard token
informational_truth.content: A cryptographic key stored on or a one-time password (OTP) transmitted to a specialized hardware device (for example, a PDA, mobile phone, smart card, USB key) rather than a general-purpose computer.
informational_truth.evidence_quote: Hard token: A cryptographic key stored on or a one-time password (OTP) transmitted to a specialized hardware device (for example, a PDA, mobile phone, smart card, USB key) rather than a general-purpose computer.

informational_truth.subject: Microsoft Authenticator app
informational_truth.content: Available on mobile phones running Android and iOS, and meets FIPS 140 Level 1 validation requirements for all Azure AD authentications.
informational_truth.evidence_quote: The Microsoft Authenticator app provides an extra level of security to your Azure AD account. It's available on mobile phones running Android and iOS... The Microsoft Authenticator app meets FIPS 140 Level 1 validation requirements for all Azure AD authentications...
